dek: Set for 25 October 2026 at Tapak Pasar Malam in Bagan Datuk, Perak, this MPTI-organised bridge run (LJSN26) offers three distances across the Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge. A local-government-backed Malaysian bridge race where the Perak River estuary and the bridge itself are the defining course features.
verdict: Larian Jambatan Sultan Nazrin Shah (LJSN26) is a local-government-organised bridge run in Bagan Datuk, Perak, a coastal district investing in sports tourism. Organised by Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI), the race offers three distances (21K, 10K, 5K). The Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge spanning the Perak River estuary provides the defining course feature: a modern, wide-span bridge with expansive estuary and Straits of Malacca views. October in Perak is the inter-monsoon period with manageable morning conditions (25-28C). Registration has not yet been announced. MPTI backing gives institutional credibility. For runners wanting a distinctive Malaysian bridge race in an under-represented part of Perak, LJSN26 is worth tracking for 25 October 2026. Monitor RaceXAsia for registration.

paragraphs: The Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge is one of Perak landmark infrastructure projects, spanning the Perak River estuary and connecting Bagan Datuk to the wider coastal region. A race centred on a landmark bridge is rare in Malaysia, and the Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge offers expansive estuary and Straits of Malacca views that no urban course can match. Organised by Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI), the municipal council for the area [1].
sections.heading: The Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge: Perak Landmark

paragraphs: Bagan Datuk is a coastal district in southwestern Perak, roughly 50 km southwest of Teluk Intan and 120 km from Ipoh. The district traditional economy is fishing and agriculture, but it is investing in sports tourism. The race starts at Tapak Pasar Malam in Bagan Datuk town, providing a central assembly area with parking and event infrastructure. For runners, Bagan Datuk offers a race location off the major-city circuit [1][2].
sections.heading: Bagan Datuk: Perak Coastal District

paragraphs: The course crosses the Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge, giving runners a distinctive out-and-back or loop configuration. The bridge deck offers panoramic estuary views at sunrise. The terrain is flat Bagan Datuk sits on the Perak coastal plain. The bridge section is elevated and exposed, so wind can be a pacing factor. Traffic is light on a Sunday morning [1].
sections.heading: The Course: Across the Bridge and Back

paragraphs: October sits in the inter-monsoon period: warm (25-28C morning) and humid (80-85 percent) with a moderate chance of afternoon thunderstorms [3]. The coastal location provides breeze off the Straits of Malacca, but the bridge section is elevated and exposed to wind. Rain typically arrives as afternoon storms that rarely trouble a morning start [3].
